items.evidence: All 24 sign block models in the vanilla 26.1 client jar are particle-only (no elements, no parent): models/block/oak_sign.json is {"textures": {"particle": "minecraft:block/oak_planks"}}; every sign blockstate points at its per-wood model; NO template_sign*.json files exist in the 26.1 jar (26.2 has them, with elements). Vanilla draws the board in the BE renderer: AbstractSignRenderer declares abstract getSignModel(S)/getSignSprite(WoodType) + submitSign (javap), StandingSignRenderer/HangingSignRenderer implement them with createSignModel/createSignLayer; BlockEntityRenderers registers SIGN + HANGING_SIGN (javap -c). The port assumes the opposite: block_entity_render.rs:366 ('the boards are block models'), :1010-1011 ('Sign boards and beds are block models in the terrain mesh'), block_entity_cem.rs:11-12; Kind::Sign (:367-371) carries text layout only and the only sign drawing code is sign_text_calls (:662). With particle-only block models the mesher emits nothing for the board, so a placed sign shows floating text only. The 26.2 withdrawal does not carry: 26.1 draws sign boards BE-side, 1.21.7-style. Sign ITEMS are unaffected (flat generated sprites in vanilla too).
items.title: Sign boards are not rendered: placed signs show floating text only (26.1 draws boards BE-side, unlike 26.2)

items.evidence: audio_harness.require_sounds() (tools/audio_harness.py:35-37) exits unless .local/horizon-client/26.1/assets/minecraft/sounds.json exists. The prepared .local (Batch 0's full prepare run, exit 0) has a complete assets/minecraft/ tree but no sounds.json and no sounds/ directory; the file is also absent from the client jar (ships only in the asset index). Root cause is prepare: sounds need the separate 'horizon-prepare sounds' subcommand (horizon-prepare/src/main.rs:240) or --complete (:276-282); Batch 0's prepare ran the export flow only. Runtime: SoundRegistry::load silently skips a missing sounds.json (horizon-client-render/src/sound_events.rs:280-282), so every event resolves to Sound::empty(). Blocks all 6 audio_harness drivers (sound_event, ambient_sound, music, situational_music, sound_engine, audio_attributes); unlike 26.2, ALL SIX are oracle-blocked as well (see B10-O04), so the sounds step alone unblocks none. The wiring spec itself is clean (1,902 sounds.json events vs 1,902 registry events; only the intentionally_empty sentinel lacks an entry, plus one vanilla orphan: entity.chicken_picky.step in sounds.json with no registry event). en_us.json IS present and md5-identical to the jar's file (98deafdb5e90e4438db30853494e1aeb, 502,008 bytes) — lang files are not missing.
items.title: No sounds.json in the prepared 26.1 resources: the game is silent and 6 audio drivers cannot run

items.evidence: Placed: vanilla 26.1 models/block/bed.json is particle-only (no elements) and every bed blockstate points at it; NO template_bed_head/foot or per-colour bed models exist in the 26.1 jar (26.2 has them). BedRenderer draws the whole bed (javap: createHeadLayer/createFootLayer, submitPiece), registered for BlockEntityType.BED (BlockEntityRenderers, javap -c; minecraft:bed IS a 26.1 block-entity type covering all 16 bed blocks, registries.json). The port has no Bed kind in block_entity_render.rs (Kind enum :322-371, classify() falls through to Kind::None at :593) and no bed drawing code anywhere in the render crates (only sleep mechanics in bed_geometry.rs / game/beds.rs), so the mesher emits nothing for a placed bed. Same wrong 'beds are block models' assumption as G01 (block_entity_render.rs:1010-1011, block_entity_cem.rs:11-12). Items: FIXED in the 26.1 port (unlike 1.21.7) — vanilla renders all 16 bed items via minecraft:composite of two minecraft:special nodes with minecraft:bed type (head + foot, items/red_bed.json); the port's SpecialModel::decode HAS a minecraft:bed arm (horizon-assets/src/item_model/special.rs:120) and the client renders it (horizon-client/src/item_render/special.rs:357, :710-713). Only the placed-bed half reproduces.
items.title: Beds are invisible when placed (bed items decode and render in the 26.1 port)

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1 registers 27 BE renderers (BlockEntityRenderers, javap -c: 26.2's 26 plus BED). The port's Kind (block_entity_render.rs:322-371) covers 13 kinds = 15 slots plus beacon beams (beacon_beam :3456, gfx/pack_entities.rs:820) = 16 slots, and classify() falls through to Kind::None for the rest (:593). Missing with visible effect (beds are B10-G03, not counted here): mob/trial spawner spinning mob (+ trial items) — cage is a block model (cube_all_inner_faces / cube_bottom_top_inner_faces), the mob is BE-rendered; campfire cooking items (logs are template_campfire, 7 elements; items BE-rendered); moving piston — moving_piston's block model is EMPTY, PistonHeadRenderer draws the moving block, so it vanishes mid-stroke (port has only collision shapes, collisions.rs:579); brushable-block brushed item (block renders via cube_all sand models); vault display item (template_vault block renders; item BE-rendered; vault.rs is server-tick logic only); shelf displayed items — ShelfRenderer registered, template_shelf_body renders the shelf but the 3 displayed items are BE-rendered and the port has only the BE data (chunk/block_entity.rs:97-98). Port has the BE data types for all six (chunk/block_entity.rs: Spawner :68, TrialSpawner :70, Vault :72, Campfire :78, Brushable :96, Shelf :98) but no rendering. Structure-block and test-instance-block renderers are also absent but their visible in-play output is unverified (both have cube block models; port has structure_block.rs / test_instance_block.rs) — noted, not claimed.
items.title: Seven vanilla block-entity renderers have no port equivalent (spawner, trial spawner, campfire, moving piston, brushable, vault, shelf)

items.evidence: REPRODUCES with the identical 1-error break as 26.2. ParityFont.java:43 calls pack.asResourceManager() on a VanillaPackResources; the method does not exist in 26.1 (error: cannot find symbol, symbol: method asResourceManager(), location: variable pack of type VanillaPackResources). Client cp: 1 error. Javap of 26.1's VanillaPackResources shows it HAS asProvider() but no asResourceManager() — repair is to build the ResourceManager from the provider. Highest-leverage single-symbol repair in the batch: ParityFont blocks 8 drivers programme-wide (7 in this batch: block_entity_render, chat_screen, hud, pack_screen, recipe_book_render, subtitle, text_display_render).
items.title: ParityFont needs VanillaPackResources.asResourceManager(), absent in 26.1 (8 drivers blocked)

Failures, all measured + javap-verified: VanillaSoundEventOracle FAIL 2e (SimpleSoundInstance.getOrResolve(SoundManager) absent :83; Sound.getAttenuationDistance takes no arguments, returns int :104) — NEW failure vs 26.2, and it cascades: VanillaSoundRig (cascade) -> VanillaMusicOracle (cascade, Batch 0 G9); VanillaSituationalMusicOracle FAIL 4e (net.minecraft.client.gui.Hud absent — 26.1 keeps the HUD in Gui); VanillaAmbientOracle FAIL 1e, VanillaSoundEngineOracle FAIL 4e, VanillaFireStarterSoundOracle FAIL 1e — all on the LocalPlayer constructor (Batch 0 G2; SoundEngine additionally needs UnderLiquidSubSound + UnderLiquidAmbientSoundInstance, both absent, 0 jar entries); VanillaAudioAttributesOracle FAIL 1e (ClockInstance :72 — exists only as the package-private nested ClientClockManager$ClockInstance / ServerClockManager$ClockInstance; no top-level class, and the nested class is not accessible outside its package, so the repair needs ClientClockManager's own API); VanillaSubtitleOracle FAIL 1e on its OWN error (Util.setTimeSource absent :188 — 26.1's Util exposes the timeSource FIELD, not a setter; NOT a cascade in 26.1, unlike 26.2); VanillaEntitySoundPacketOracle FAIL 3e (MinecraftServer ctor, Batch 0 G6 :62 — 26.1 takes 10 args incl. items.evidence: com.mojang.renderpearl.* appears ZERO times in the 26.1 client jar — the render-pipeline API the 26.3-derived oracles use does not exist in 26.1. Eight oracles import it (Batch 0 G5): VanillaHudOracle 34e (RenderPipeline :4; net.minecraft.client.gui.Hud absent :16 — 26.1 keeps the HUD in Gui; contextualbar.ExperienceBar absent :17 — only ExperienceBarRenderer exists; LocalPlayer ctor G2 :133), VanillaPackScreenOracle 13e (RenderPipeline; text-input no-overrides :224-226; Gui ctor takes only Minecraft :246; setScreen/screen() no-override :247/:261; Language.DEFAULT_INSTANCE absent :309/:323 — 26.1's Language has only the DEFAULT string), VanillaRecipeBookScreenOracle 4e (RenderPipeline only), VanillaLoomScreenOracle 5e (RenderPipeline + Hud :68), VanillaWorldBorderRenderOracle 34e (GpuBuffer, CommandEncoder, RenderPass, GpuDevice, RenderPipeline :5-9, plus Hud :19 and DynamicGpuData :21, 0 jar entries), VanillaSpriteAnimationOracle 2e (GpuBufferSlice; driver test_sprite_animation_parity outside this batch's 50, recorded here as render-family), VanillaTranslucencyOracle 4e (IndexType + MeshData.decodeQuadCentroids absent :26 + SortState.writeSortedIndexBuffer absent :50; driver outside this batch's 50), VanillaTabListOracle 36e (authlib.services.* 8 imports — absent from authlib 7.0.63, Batch 0 G7 — + RenderPipeline :21 + Hud :32 + world.scores.TeamColor :53 — 26.1 has only client.color.item.TeamColor; driver outside this batch's 50). Five more fail on neighbouring 26.3-only APIs: VanillaChatScreenOracle 5e (Hud :20/:278-279 + CommandSourceStack.getAvailablePostEffects() absent :120), VanillaMenuOracle 4e (net.minecraft.util.Prediction absent :138; DedicatedServer ctor takes 8 args, oracle passes 10 nulls :65; EntityTypes.PLAYER G4 :128-129; cascades VanillaRecipeBookOracle + VanillaPlaceRecipeOracle, cross-ref Batch 4/7), ServerPackClient 1e (no-override :264; driver test_server_resource_pack_parity outside this batch's 50, cross-ref Batch 11 — coordinator to assign). Drivers blocked in this batch: hud, pack_screen, recipe_book_render, screen_layout, world_border_render, chat_screen (compiles VanillaPackScreenOracle as a dependency), menu_click (7). Repair is a 26.3-to-26.1 backport: 26.1 screens render through the SubmitNodeCollector/RenderType path (GuiGraphics), not a GPU pipeline object, and 26.1's HUD lives in Gui. The family's other members, measured: VanillaContainerScreenOracle and VanillaOptionsOracle PASS on the client cp; VanillaPackSelectionOracle and VanillaRecipeBookViewOracle also PASS (drivers outside this batch's 50).

method: javap on the named 26.1 client jar (26.1.x/versions/26.1/jars/client.jar, Mojang-mapped, 10,682 classes) for every vanilla class in scope, plus the named server-game jar (26.1.x/versions/26.1/jars/server-game.jar, 7,351 classes) for server-side classes; exhaustive jar-asset scans (all 1,506 item definitions incl. nested model nodes; sign/bed/spawner/campfire/vault/shelf/piston/brushable block models and blockstates; BE renderer registration via javap -c on BlockEntityRenderers); 1,902-event sounds.json fetched sha1-verified from Mojang's asset index 30 into the batch evidence dir for the wiring diff only; source comparison against versions/26.1/crates/ on parity-sweep-26.1; prepared-data check of .local/horizon-client/26.1/ (Batch 0's prepare run, GATE OK); and oracle status from the measured Batch 0 table (docs/sweep/26.1/batch-0-oracles.json, fixpoint big-compile) plus the Batch 0 driver map (b0/drivers.json) — every failing oracle's full error text was read in b0/big-compile-client.log and every missing symbol/package/constructor was javap-verified against the 26.1 jars by this batch; no import-level oracle check was used. NO driver runs and NO cargo tests: checks-only batch. 50 drivers triaged by measured status (16 runnable, 31 oracle-blocked, 3 no-oracle server-e2e); 12 behaviour checks resolved statically (8 pass, 4 gap); oracle triage counted separately (38 failing in-scope oracles across 4 items).

source: docs/PARITY-SWEEP.md §4 Batch 10 — checks only, no fixes. Scope: models, block-entity rendering, screens, sound wiring, options; 50 drivers + static checks. 26.1 run: oracle status from the measured Batch 0 table only (no import-level check — the 26.2 run's B10 failure was not repeated); report completeness verified by reading the tail before reporting.
systemic_note: Three systemic patterns, all different from 26.2. (1) The sign/bed form FLIPPED between 26.1 and 26.2: 26.1 still draws sign boards and beds in BE renderers (1.21.7-style, particle-only block models), while 26.2 moved them to block models — so the 26.2 withdrawals of B10-G01/B10-G03 do NOT carry, and the port's inherited 26.3 assumption ('boards and beds are block models') is wrong for 26.1 in both cases. The 26.1 port fixed the bed-ITEM half during the port (minecraft:bed decode + draw path exist) but not the placed-bed half. (2) 26.1 predates several 26.2 APIs the oracles assume — the Hud class split out of Gui, the EntityTypes holder move, FirstPersonHandsAndItems, shadeDirectionOverride, the x()/getX() packet-accessor renames — on top of the 26.3-only APIs (renderpearl, UvMapping, DynamicGpuData, asResourceManager, ClockInstance-as-top-level-class). Result: 31 of 50 drivers oracle-blocked (vs 22 for 26.2), all 6 audio drivers blocked on oracles AND data, and the sound oracle family itself broken at its root (VanillaSoundEventOracle). (3) The sound stack is blocked on data AND oracles: Batch 0's prepare ran the export flow only, so the prepared 26.1 resources have no sounds.json — one 'horizon-prepare sounds' run fixes the silent game but unblocks NO audio driver until the sound oracles are repaired too (unlike 26.2, where 3 were oracle-clean). The wiring spec itself is clean (1,902/1,902 real events, plus one vanilla orphan: entity.chicken_picky.step exists in sounds.json with no registry event).
